text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a positive assessment of the economy, published yesterday in its quarterly Bulletin, the Reserve Bank predicted that the struggling retail sector is poised to recover and it firmly ruled out an interest cut for now. The report said stronger consumer spnding would play a large part in helping growth accelerate in 1997. Page 1.

Thanks to a A$1 billion gold hedging policy, which allowed it to get A$598 an ounce from its 710,000 ounces of gold sales despite a slump in world bullion prices, as well as an improved performance by its zinc interests, Australia's largest gold miner, Normandy Mining Ltd, has posted a 9.3 per cent increase in interim net profit to A$51.6 million. Page 1.

The Australian corporate bond market has staged a dramatic revival as companies seek to take advantage of low interest rates and a large increase in demand from investors, with new issues of bonds this year set to substantially exceed the A$1.3 billion rased in the late 1980s, the only other period of significant activity in the market. Page 1.

Responding to Woolworths Ltd's announcement of plans to dramatically lift its share of the wholesale market, Joint managing director of grocery wholesaler and retailer Davids Ltd , John Patten, said yesterday there was no room for another wholesaler in Autralia, and he said Davids would launch a price war if Woolworths pursues its plans. Page 17.

After one year in the hot-seat at engineering company ANI, Peter Stancliffe has, with the help of last year's McKinsey and Co strategic review, developed a clearly defined growth plan, which he believes will see the engineering company readmitted to the eite ranks of Australia's top blue-chip listed stocks within five years. Page 17.

Australian National Industries Ltd yesterday delivered a 31 per cent increase in interim net profit for the December half based on strong earnings gains from its steel businesses and the absence of large writedowns from its disastrous investment in the Euopean environmental engineering group Holter, but has halved its dividend to just one-cent-a-share as it continues to be plagued by the Holter investment. Page 17.
THE AUSTRALIAN

As analysts and investors applaud its ambitious push into the A$10 billion-a-year wholesale grocery distribution market, Woolworths shares climbed 20 cents yesterday to close at a record high of A$3.59 on heavy volume of 6.99 million shares - a result whih added more than A$220 million to the value of the blue-chip retailer. Page 19.

In a wide-ranging speech to a Securities Institute luncheon in Melbourne yesterday, RTZ-CRA managing director Leigh Clifford said the inadequacies of the Native Title Act were highlighted last week when six months of negotiations with Queensland Gulf Aborginal claimants over the development of RTZ-CRA's A$1.1 billion Century Zinc project collapsed, he has called for a six-month time limit to the native title claims process. Page 19.

There were signs of recovery yesterday for heavy engineering group Australian National Industries Ltd which recorded a 213 percent rise in December half profit to A$16.4 million. This improvement was marred however by a further A$14.5 million loss at its Holter engineering division in Europe which halved the company's interim dividend to 1c. Page 19

Commenting on a recent survey that found a degree of derivative speculation in the management of Australia's A$260 billion superannuation industry, Insurance and Superannuation Commissioner George Pooley warned yesterday that trustees of super funds needed to remember that investments in derivatives speculation was not consistent with the prudent person rule governing super fund investments. Page 19

The Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) February Bulletin released yesterday affirmed that economic growth was growing and that monetary policy was on hold. The announcement sent share prices soaring with the dollar being strengthened. The RBA also repeated a warning made by the central bank governor, Ian Macfarlane, that the next move in official interest rates would depend on wages growth. Page 19

Telecom Corp of NZ has announced it is abandoning its Pacific Star business in Australia. The company recorded an 8.2 per cent slide in its December net profits to from PacStar to NZ$17.3. The PacStar closure comes after a major review of its investment ommitment following adverse changes to Telstra pricing policies in Australia. Telecom still hopes to continue business in Australia servicing the needs of large corporate customers operating in Australia and New Zealand. Page 21 -
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a finding that was a significant factor in the Reserve bank's highly optimistic assessment of the Australian economy, the central bank's latest quarterly report says corporate Australia's financial well-being will be a key factor in driving the economy towards sustained growth. Page 31.

Despite production difficulties at Port Kembla, where the shutdown of a blast furnace in January resulted in a two-week shutdown and a six-day annual maintenance shutdown of the Sydney Steel mill, BHP's steel division is showing signs of breaking a protrated slump, with January production figures, released yesterday, revealing that sales over the past year have improved. Page 31.

The Australian Securities Commission has written to the board of John Fairfax Holdings raising questions about a report by Fairfax's independent expert - Price Waterhouse - on Brierley Investment's proposal to buy a 4.9 per cent stake from Conrad Black's ollinger group. Page 31.

Thanks to strong investment markets and benefits from restructuring, Perpetual Trustees Australia saw its December-half after-tax profit rise 87.1 per cent to A$11.76 million, including abnormals, and its net profit before abnormals rise 28.5 per cent to $8.45 million. Page 33.

According to a survey by the Investment Funds Association, net funds totalling A$7.9 billion poured into share funds and managed investments run by IFA members last year. The survey showed IFA members are responsible for 92 to 95 per cent of retail funds nvested and 50 to 55 per cent of wholesale funds. Page 33.

After revealing earlier this month that it had undertaken a review of all its assets ahead of a major restructuring, it is understood CSR has been in talks with New Zealand forestry giant Carter Holt Harvey and the two groups are said to be close to carvig out a deal on the sale or joint venture of CSR's A$1 billion timber business. Page 33.
THE AGE

The Reserve Bank's latest quarterly report on the economy has virtually ruled out any imminent change in interest rates, saying the Reserve predicts the economy will quicken this year and if its optimistic scenario for the next two years is realised, the report implies that no change in interest rates is likely this year. Page C1.

Government owned Rosvoorouzhenie, which is the main export supplier of hardware from the former Soviet Union's vast armaments industry, is visiting Australia for the first time and will set out its stall at a press conference at the Australian Internationl Air Show in Victoria, where it hopes to sell missiles, submarines, fighter aircraft tanks and rocket launchers. Page C1.

Australia's biggest gold producer Normandy Mining, has posted a 9.3 per cent increase in its December half profit to A$51.6 million, which compares favourably with the previous profit level of A$47.2 million. The rise has been attributed to a A$250 millin capital expenditure program which Normandy has implemented over the last eighteen months and which has resulted in lower operating costs in major operations. Page C3.

Recording a A$16.4 million net profit, Australian National Industries is confident it is on the road to recovery. The result was a massive improvement from the A$5.2 million recorded in the first half of last year. The ANI share price increased five cens to A$1.30 in expectation of continued profit growth and analysts have welcomed moves by ANI to dispose of its unsuccessful environmental engineering business, Hoelter. Page C3.

Exploration results from accelerated drilling at Mineral Commodities NL's White Foil site, twenty two kilometres west of Kalgoorlie, have increased expectations of a one million ounce-plus gold discovery. A preliminary resource estimate for the first excvated zone is due in July with technical work starting now. Page C3.

Strong investment markets and restructuring benefits have pushed Perpetual Trustees Australia's December-half after-tax profit up 87.1 per cent to A$11.76 million, including abnormals. Directors are confident the fully franked interim dividend, up 14 cens to 18 cents, will achieve a final dividend of 22 cents. Page C3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
